﴿Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind"﴾, the Creator and Owner of them. They were singled out for mention to honour them, and as a fitting link to seeking protection from the evil of the whisperer (al-Muwaswis) in their breasts.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 114, verse 3:

﴿Ilahi l-nas (the God of mankind)﴾ are either two substitutes (badal), two descriptive qualifiers (sifat), or an appositive clarification (atf bayan), and the genitive noun (al-mudaf ilayhi), which is "mankind," is repeated explicitly in them for the sake of clarification.

From the evil of the whisperer (al-waswas), the Shayṭān, who is called "the whisperer" (al-ḥadath) because of how constantly he is associated with it, the one who slinks back (al-khannās), because he withdraws and draws back from the heart whenever Allah is mentioned.
﴿Who whispers into the breasts of people﴾: their hearts, when they are heedless of the remembrance of God.

from the jinn and mankind. This clarifies that the whisperer (al-shaytan al-muwaswis) is both jinn and human, like His saying, "devils of mankind and jinn" [6:112]; or "from the jinn" clarifies it, and "mankind" is conjoined to "the whisperer," and each encompasses the evil of Labid and his daughters mentioned [in the hadith]. The first view was objected to on the grounds that mankind does not whisper into the breasts of people; rather, it is the jinn who whisper into their breasts. It was answered that mankind also whispers, in a sense appropriate to them outwardly, and then their whispering reaches the heart and becomes fixed in it through the path that leads to that. And God the Exalted knows best.
